name: Pictorial Superiority Effect
fact: Pictures access semantic information more readily than name information, while words access articulatory information more rapidly than pictures.

provenance.title: Conditions for a Picture-Superiority Effect on Consumer Memory
provenance.quote_or_locus: The results indicate that picture superiority occurs in both immediate and delayed recall tasks when processing is directed at appearance features

provenance.title: Tracing the time course of picture-word processing.
provenance.quote_or_locus: These experiments suggest a model of information access whereby pictures access semantic information were readily than name information, with the reverse being true for words

provenance.title: Pictorial superiority effect.
provenance.quote_or_locus: High schematic similarity eliminated the pictorial superiority effects at the slow rate and completely reversed it at the fast rate
